result.title: Physically Guided TeX Generation for Low-Light Visual Tasks
result.summary: Low-light conditions reduce visible contrast and obscure details, while infrared images lack color and texture, motivating the fusion of infrared and visible information for visual tasks. Existing fusion methods primarily optimize image appearance or task-specific features without explicitly disentangling the coupled factors underlying thermal observations, limiting their physical interpretation under thermal degeneracy. Hyperspectral thermal measurements enable physical decomposition, but they require specialized imaging hardware, while pixel-level physical annotations for supervision or evaluation incur additional costs. We propose TeX-Gen, a physically guided framework for TeX generation from paired visible and infrared images in low-light visual tasks. TeX Generation constructs complementary multi-view features and employs independent branch-specific gates to route cues into the Temperature, Emissivity, and Texture maps. TeXMetric integrates radiometric reconstruction, channel structure, and material consistency to assess the generated maps without requiring pixel-level physical labels. TeX Tune improves performance through task-guided adjustments, jointly optimizing the adjustment modules and task network while keeping the generator frozen. Experiments show that TeX-Gen achieves competitive task performance in low-light environments on the FLIR, LLVIP, M3FD, and MSRS datasets. Experiments on HADAR also examine the association between TeXMetric scores and downstream detection performance.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 TeX-Gen，从成对可见光与红外图像生成温度、发射率与纹理图，并给出无需像素级物理标注的 TeXMetric 及冻结生成器下的任务引导微调，在低光检测任务上验证效果。
AI.relevance_reason: 其用独立门控分支将多视角线索路由为解耦物理图，并以无标签复合指标评估分解质量、在冻结生成器下做任务引导微调，可能为 latent 状态的证据筛选、内容评估与任务导向监督提供类比线索，可供核查。
